narrative:
On October 28, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 35.4%, with 1,051 cases heard out of 2,968 scheduled across 52 judges. This reflects a notable decrease from the previous court day on October 27, when the court achieved a 48.7% clearance rate, hearing 1,423 of 2,923 matters.

Performance varied considerably across court halls. Justice S Vishwajith Shetty in Hall 21 marked one of the highest throughputs among substantial rosters, hearing 69 of 95 scheduled matters (72.6%). Justice V Srishananda in Hall 23 also demonstrated strong activity, taking up 54 of 79 cases (68.4%), while Justice G Basavaraja in Hall 32 heard 52 of 86 matters (60.5%). Conversely, certain rosters experienced acute bottlenecks; Justice C.M. Poonacha in Hall 31 heard just 7 of 118 cases (5.9%), a sharp decline from October 27 when the bench disposed of 87.5% of its 40-case board. Additionally, Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum in Hall 14 managed only 4 of 49 matters (8.2%).

Procedurally, Admission stages maintained higher throughput than substantive disposals. The court converted 43.9% of Admission matters (353 heard of 805 scheduled) and 48.1% of Further Hearings (26 of 54). In contrast, Orders conversion fell significantly from 53.3% on October 27 to 33.6% today (344 heard of 1,025). Final Hearings remained low at 24.9% (129 of 519), down from 31.9% the prior day.

By case type, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the bulk of the docket with 1,309 listings, recording a 33.8% hearing rate (443 heard)—a drop from the 45.2% recorded on October 27. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) saw 195 of 540 matters heard (36.1%), falling from the previous day's 55.3%. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) also contracted sharply to 31.5% (94 of 298), compared to 56.6% on October 27.
